title: Publish coherent metadata generations
objective: UI, search, dictionaries and machine tools consume the same accepted generation.
outcome: Publication-manifest closure rejects missing assets, source-context mismatches and undeclared partial fragments. A historical Pennsylvania published-record count cannot appear as current coverage. A large dictionary is paged predictably; one bad asset does not blank the entire catalog. No request mixes old catalog records with a new dictionary. Failed publication leaves the last good version live. Static fallback remains a tested recovery option. Sealed packages/search/publication-lifecycle-v2.mjs is not edited.

commits.subject: Assemble the accepted publication manifest
commits.instructions: Include canonical revisions, dictionary bindings, examples, source cards, coverage, search projection and contract versions. Reconcile the Sources page v1.1.0 national-readiness table with the current generation: migrate supported facts or explicitly archive that historical view. Reuse immutable publication/checksum machinery.
commits.verification: Manifest closure rejects missing assets, source-context mismatches and undeclared partial fragments; a historical Pennsylvania published-record count cannot appear as current coverage.

commits.subject: Integrate bounded content delivery
commits.instructions: Serve only needed record/dictionary/example pages through existing repository ports. Measure asset-count and response-size consequences before selecting a storage transition.
commits.verification: A large dictionary is paged predictably; one bad asset does not blank the entire catalog.

commits.subject: Verify generation promotion and rollback
commits.instructions: Compare every public projection against the accepted source revision and publish only after closure checks. Exercise N-1 retrieval and typed expired-generation behavior.
commits.verification: No request mixes old catalog records with a new dictionary; failed publication leaves the last good version live.
